newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy slams Israeli trade policy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy slams Israeli trade policy.

text.p: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk on Sunday sharply criticised Israeli trade policy, saying the Jewish state had an obligation to step up imports from the United States.

"You owe it to us. It's an important way to reciprocate our friendship and support, although we give it freely," Indyk said in a speech before the U.S.-Israel Chamber of Commerce also attended by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"The problem is that you have a huge deficit in your trading relationship with Europe and you should share some of that with the U.S.," he said, noting that the United States accounted for 20 percent of imports to Israel versus Europe's 50 percent.
Israel's trade minister said recently that Israel's chronic trade deficit with Europe reached about $10 billion last year.
Indyk was critical of Israeli policy regarding government tenders. He said U.S. contractors felt the process was unfair.

He also faulted Israel's failing to respect intellectual property rights and noted that Israel had been placed on the U.S. trade representative's list of countries under surveillance for violating copyright and other related matters.
Israel was added to the list in April. A U.S. embassy spokesman said that Israeli actions would be monitored but there was no immediate threat of countervailing action.
Indyk said Israeli technical standards and packaging rules "unfairly discriminate against U.S. products". He said Israel had repeatedly promised to take action but nothing had happened.
He added Israeli insurance rates discriminated against U.S.-made cars.
And he scored Israel's food import policy for banning both kosher and non-kosher meat imports -- kosher meat being that slaughtered according to Jewish ritual law.
Israel should allow imports of kosher U.S. meat, he said, describing a ban on kosher imports as "not fair, pure and simple."
